summary: Implemented create_device/update_device/delete_device with strict validation, via a new application::device_service layer (commands -> application -> domain -> storage). Extended Device::validate() to also validate each service's name and URL (http/https only). create_device generates a UUID id and RFC3339 timestamps; update_device preserves id/created_at while bumping updated_at and 404s on an unknown id; delete_device 404s if nothing was removed; all three validate before ever touching disk, so invalid input never persists or corrupts the existing device list. 12 new Rust unit tests, 43 total passing.
completed: domain/device.rs: Device::validate() now also validates each registered service's name (non-empty) and url (must parse and use http or https; rejects javascript:, file:, data:, and malformed URLs).
application/device_service.rs: DeviceInput (editable fields only, no client-settable id/createdAt/updatedAt) + create_device/update_device/delete_device.
create_device: generates a UUID v4 id and matching RFC3339 created_at/updated_at (via chrono), validates, then persists.
update_device: looks up the existing device by id (NotFound if missing), preserves id and created_at, bumps updated_at, validates, then persists; a rejected update never touches the stored list.
delete_device: removes by id, NotFound if nothing was removed.

commands/devices.rs: create_device/update_device/delete_device Tauri commands, mapping DeviceServiceError to the existing ApplicationError (ValidationError/NotFoundError/StorageError); registered in lib.rs.
src/types/device.ts + src/lib/tauri/devices.ts: added DeviceInput type and createDevice/updateDevice/deleteDevice wrappers.
Added uuid, chrono, and url as direct Cargo dependencies.
12 new Rust unit tests (5 domain service-URL/name validation, 7 application-layer create/update/delete including rejected-input-doesn't-persist cases), for 43 total.
Verified cargo test (43/43), cargo build, npm run build, and npm run lint all pass.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Invalid host/port/username/service URL values are rejected with a clear ApplicationError
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: create_rejects_invalid_input_without_persisting and update_rejects_invalid_input_leaving_original_untouched tests; commands map DeviceServiceError::Validation to ApplicationError{code: "ValidationError", ...}.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Shell metacharacters in any field are rejected
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Host/username shell-metacharacter rejection was already covered in WU005; this work unit adds the equivalent guard for service URLs (only http/https schemes accepted, via url::Url::parse + scheme check) so a service URL can't be used to smuggle a dangerous scheme either.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Rust unit tests cover valid and invalid input cases
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: 12 new tests across domain::device (service URL/name validation) and application::device_service (create/update/delete success and failure paths, including that a rejected create/update never persists).

notes: Risk score: 25/100 (low-medium). Rationale: this is the first work unit that actually mutates persisted device state via commands; the two things that could silently corrupt data -- a validation failure sneaking through to save_all(), or an update losing the original id/created_at -- are both directly unit-tested (rejected input leaves the stored list byte-for-byte unchanged; update preserves id/created_at while only updated_at changes). No SSH/network surface is touched yet.
UI forms to actually call these commands are explicitly out of scope per this work unit and land in WU008 (connection testing command and device forms UI).
